Certified passport copies and proof of address for all general partners, limited partners and ultimate beneficial owners

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening against the United Nations, OFAC, EU, UK (OFSI) and Bermuda sanctions lists, plus enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs), adverse media, negative reputational coverage and unexplained wealth flags. Screening must be completed for each general partner, limited partner and UBO before registration; results documented in the AML/CFT compliance file and retained for at least five years. Any match is escalated for senior management and the Bermuda Financial Intelligence Agency is notified where required under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1997.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Companies Registry Online Name Search and Reservation Portal (https://www.gov.bm/companies-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in Roman characters and the English language. The statutory name of an Exempted Limited Partnership must end with 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.' or 'LP'. Non-Roman script cannot be used; brand names in other languages must be romanized/transliterated before submission.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An extension request in writing must be lodged with the Registrar of Companies before the expiry of the initial 30-day reservation window. If the name is rejected, the applicant or its Bermuda counsel shall file a written administrative appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days stating the grounds on which the proposed name complies with the Exempted Partnerships Act 2015 and comparable corporate name rules. Where the Registrar confirms refusal, further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Bermuda under Order 55 of the Rules of the Supreme Court 1973. Time limits are strict and professional guidance is required at every step.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a purely online fashion jewelry and timepiece merchandising business only if the ELP appoints a licensed registered agent and maintains a physical registered office in Bermuda. A mail-forwarding or virtual point address cannot satisfy the statutory registered office requirement; the licensed service provider may use its own physical premises for this purpose. No local employees, assets or physical premises are otherwise mandated for an Exempted Limited Partnership.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 5% probability per annum of an unannounced inspection or regulatory query from the BMA or Registrar for a medium-risk e-commerce ELP. The probability rises to 15% or greater if the entity is flagged in a PEP/sanctions review, receives adverse media, or establishes banking relationships with high-risk correspondent institutions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Exempted Partnerships Act 2014 (Bermuda), as amended, ss. 4-9 (registration, name, general partner, registered office, principal representative and register of partners) and s. 12 (effect of registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Exempted Partnership Application for Registration (Form ELP-1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Bermuda law imposes no minimum paid-up capital for an exempted limited partnership. The partnership agreement governs the amount, timing and form of capital contributions, and there is no statutory escrow account requirement. Where the partnership accepts customer settlement funds before delivery, such funds must be held in a designated client-money account with a licensed bank or authorised payment institution; escrow terms imposed by payment processors are contractual rather than statutory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the General Partner, acting as the board-equivalent governing body of [●] Exempted Limited Partnership (the "Partnership"), hereby (1) adopts the executed Partnership Agreement; (2) accepts the initial capital contributions as set out in the capital account; (3) approves the registered office at [●], Hamilton, Bermuda, with [●] as its registered agent; and (4) appoints [●] as Principal Resident Representative and [●] as AML Compliance Officer. RESOLVED FURTHER that the General Partner authorises the Registrar filing, the opening of merchant settlement accounts with Stripe and PayPal, and the execution of all ancillary formation, banking, and e-commerce contracts. RESOLVED FINALLY that any two authorised officers may certify and deliver documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Partnership Agreement Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda, via Gov.bm online e-services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name through the Registrar's online name-clearance module, including the mandatory legal-form suffix "Exempted Limited Partnership" or "E.L.P.". The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name on the Bermuda register. Concurrently execute the partnership agreement and obtain written consent from the proposed Bermuda-licensed registered office provider.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered office
Certified identification documents of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused on similarity grounds, submit two alternative names within 10 working days; any refusal may be reviewed by the Registrar on written application with a formal representation letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarisation of General Partner Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda notary public / Deputy Registrar of Companies receiving the notarial pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a statutory declaration of the general partner verifying the partnership's name, registered office, capital contributions, principal representative and compliance with the domestic-business restrictions of the Exempted Partnerships Act 2014. Execute before a notary public; if executed abroad, legalise by apostille or consular legalisation. Deliver the notarial pack to the Bermuda registered agent.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation or passport of the general partner
KYC record of the principal resident representative
AML source-of-funds evidence for initial contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is deficient or not legalised, re-execute and re-notarise; where the Registrar rejects the foreign certificate, obtain a fresh apostille from the issuing state within 90 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration Application and Payment of Government Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Bermuda (Gov.bm e-filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form ELP-1 with the Registrar together with the executed partnership agreement, statutory declaration and registered-office consent. Pay the non-refundable government registration fee of BD$1,480 (US$1,480 equivalent) online and retain the automated receipt. The Registrar will examine the application for legislative compliance and issue the certificate upon approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition, respond within 21 days with an amended filing; if the application is rejected, correct the defects and re-file with a fresh fee; if no response after 5 working days, escalate by formal letter to the Senior Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate and Adoption of Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download or collect the Certificate of Registration of Exempted Limited Partnership. Immediately convene the first meeting of the general partner to pass the pro-forma first board-equivalent resolution, adopt the register of partners and register of charges, and issue executed capital-account statements to each limited partner.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, apply to the Registrar for a certificate of correction; if the certificate is not issued within 7 business days after filing, request expedition through the Ministry of Finance customer service desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Designation of Principal Resident Representative and Bermuda Regulatory Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies and the Ministry of Finance; Bermuda Monetary Authority where exchange control applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Principal Resident Representative appointment form and the registered-office address update with the Registrar. If the exempted partnership claims exempt status under the Exchange Control Act, complete the required approval with the Bermuda Monetary Authority. Submit any AML compliance appointments under the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2018. No Bermuda income-tax registration is required because Bermuda levies no income tax; however, apply for a tax reference or non-residence certificate if needed for banking or treaty purposes.
required_dossiers: Non-resident tax certificate application if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry queries the exchange-control or AML filing, respond with supporting statutory declarations; if the principal representative disclaims office, appoint a replacement within 14 days and file the change with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank, Payment Provider and Physical-Site Licensing Checks
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority regulated institutions; Department of Environment and Natural Resources; Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service if physical premises are used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a segregated merchant settlement account with a Bermuda-licensed bank, EMI or an approved foreign acquiring bank. Complete Stripe and PayPal onboarding using the registered legal name of the exempted limited partnership and the certificate of registration. Confirm that no Business Licences Act operating licence is needed where sales are exclusively online and exported. If a physical fulfilment area is used, submit a Low-Impact Business Permit application to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources and a fire-safety structural clearance to the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service before stocking goods.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration and partnership deed
General partner identity and AML file
Bank reference or alternative financial history for payment processor
Premises fire-safety and structural completion statement if a warehouse is leased
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If banking or payment-provider onboarding is suspended, re-submit an enhanced KYC pack including the certificate, partnership agreement and source of wealth, and apply to an alternative licensed EMI; if fire-safety clearance is withheld, remedy the identified defect and re-inspect within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy and Labour - Department of Commerce / Business Licensing Unit; Department of Environment and Natural Resources for environmental matters
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - Exempted Limited Partnership engaged solely in cross-border online retail of fine jewelry, watches and fashion accessories; no Bermuda Business Licence or industrial operating permit is required for distance selling without a physical retail shop or manufacturing facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Government of Bermuda
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 - Exempt / Low Impact: administrative registration only; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required for online sales, warehousing below 500 m², or activities involving no land disturbance or construction.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC emission is generated by digital retail. Any packaging waste generated must comply with the Waste Management Regulations 2016. If a fulfilment site stores volatile cleaning solvents, solvent storage must not exceed 5 litres and must comply with the Dangerous Goods (Storage and Transport) Regulations 2013.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-safety certificate is required for a registered office without public access. For a leased fulfilment space, a Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service clearance and a structural load inspection under the Bermuda Building Code 2014 are required before occupancy. If five or more employees work physically in Bermuda, the Department of Labour must issue an Occupational Safety and Health clearance before operations commence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Bermuda: Office of the Tax Commissioner (OTC) — official portal https://taxcommissioner.gov.bm; Registrar of Companies — https://www.roc.gov.bm. United Kingdom: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) — https://www.gov.uk/vat-registration for UK VAT registration of the overseas ELP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Bermuda levies no income tax, capital gains tax, or VAT, so no general TIN/VAT ID is issued. The ELP obtains its statutory identity by: (1) registering under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992 with the Registrar of Companies, obtaining a Registered Number and Certificate of Formation; (2) filing annually for a 'Certificate of Compliance' within 30 days of each anniversary as proof of good standing; (3) registering with the OTC for Payroll Tax and Social Insurance (obtaining a Payroll Tax Registration Number) only if it has Bermuda-resident employees; (4) obtaining automatic Exchange Control 'Standard Consent' from the Bermuda Monetary Authority as a foreign-owned non-resident entity, permitting USD/BMD foreign-currency bank accounts; (5) for UK supply-side activities, registering online for UK VAT via HMRC's 'Register for VAT' service using the Bermuda Registered Number as the corporate identifier, with HMRC assigning a GB VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible / Territorial_Scope / Tax_Exempt_Zone. The Bermuda ELP is fiscally transparent; each partner is taxed on its share of profits by residence (a UK corporate partner is charged under UK CTA 2009 Part 5). Bermuda imposes no tax on worldwide or Bermuda-source income, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax, and no indirect tax. The ELP benefits from the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, guaranteeing immunity from any future Bermuda income or capital tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Bermuda has no check-the-box regime. Available elections: (1) under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992, the Partnership Agreement may elect that the ELP have separate legal personality or remain a pure contractual partnership; (2) under the Economic Substance Act 2018, an ELP carrying on a 'relevant activity' may elect to be treated as tax resident in another jurisdiction if centrally managed and controlled there, but online retail distribution of jewelry and timepieces is not a relevant activity, so no economic substance filing is required; (3) under UK Part 6A TIOPA 2010 hybrid-mismatch rules, the ELP is treated as transparent, and a UK parent must ensure deductible payments (e.g., management fees or financing) made to the ELP are matched by corresponding UK inclusions to prevent deduction denial, as Bermuda imposes no tax on the ELP's receipt.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Bermuda: No VAT, GST, or Sales and Use Tax; import customs duties and stamp duty apply at the border. United Kingdom (supply-side nexus): UK VAT at 20% standard rate applies to the ELP's online sales of jewelry and timepieces to UK consumers; the ELP is an 'overseas seller' and is the deemed supplier for low-value consignments not exceeding GBP 135, and the importer of record for higher-value goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Bermuda: BMD 0 — no indirect tax registration threshold. UK: GBP 0 mandatory registration for non-established sellers of imported goods in consignments not exceeding GBP 135 to UK consumers (no turnover threshold); GBP 90,000 threshold for other taxable supplies made by an overseas person, effective from 1 April 2024.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Bermuda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime. UK: Making Tax Digital (MTD) for VAT is mandatory — the ELP must maintain digital records and file VAT returns via MTD-compatible software through HMRC APIs; no real-time HMRC clearance or e-invoicing stamping requirement exists. Commercial e-invoicing (e.g., PEPPOL) is contractual, not statutory, for this B2C jewelry/fashion online trade.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Bermuda: N/A — no VAT is chargeable on exports from Bermuda, so zero-rating is inapplicable. UK: If the ELP registers for UK VAT and sells goods to customers outside the UK, zero-rating applies where the goods are exported from the UK to a third-country destination (including Bermuda) within 3 months of the sale, and the ELP holds prescribed export evidence; zero-rating also applies to certain services related to goods supplied to overseas recipients who belong outside the UK. For internet sales imported directly into the UK from Bermuda, zero-rating is not available; the point-of-sale import VAT rules instead apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (UK CDS export entry with MRN reference evidencing departure from GB)
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) proving physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank/FX receipt evidencing payment from the overseas buyer into the ELP's Bermuda or UK account)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (itemized jewelry/timepiece descriptions, values, and HS codes)
Proof of Export (P2P) documentation where simplified declarations are used
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may issue VAT assessments for 4 years (extended to 20 years for deliberate or concealed conduct), plus inaccuracy penalties of 30% to 100% of the VAT loss under Schedule 24 FA 2007. Unsupported zero-rating claims trigger retrospective clawback of output VAT at 20% plus interest under section 73 VATA 1994. Fraudulent export claims may lead to criminal prosecution under section 72 VATA 1994 and civil penalties of up to 100% of the evaded VAT. Bermuda: no indirect-tax clawback exists; however, the OTC may audit payroll tax and impose penalties of up to 25% of the underpaid amount plus interest for non-compliant employers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) acting under the Bermuda Exchange Control Act 1972, the Banks and Deposit Companies Act 1999, and the Bermuda Companies Act; the BMA is the central bank and exchange control administrator for the Bermudian dollar (BMD).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermudian dollar is pegged at 1:1 to the United States dollar, and US dollars circulate freely as legal tender. Capital-account and current-account transactions are freely convertible for an Exempted Limited Partnership that has been granted non-resident exchange-control status by the BMA, a status automatically obtainable for entities registered under the Exempted Partnerships Act 2009 and used exclusively for business outside Bermuda. Profit remittance in the form of distributions and capital redemptions to non-resident partners faces no BMA approval hurdle provided the ELP's partner contribution registers are correctly endorsed; if the partnership were instead classified as resident for exchange-control purposes, prior BMA consent would be required for each remittance, which is unlikely given the intended e-commerce business scope.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For an ELP designated as non-resident, export proceeds arising from online jewelry and watch sales are not subject to mandatory surrender to an authorised dealer, and may be retained in foreign-currency or BMD/USD accounts. Any resident-registered entity would be required under the Exchange Control Regulations to surrender export receipts within one month unless granted a specific non-resident designation or exemption. As the target ELP operates wholly outside Bermuda and intends to obtain non-resident exchange-control status, the surrender time-limit is not applicable; however, the general partner must maintain a current certificate of non-resident status from the BMA to avoid any future requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium for cross-border payment-service integration; Low for core banking. Bermuda does not licence domestic electronic money institutions, and only entities licensed under the Banks and Deposit Companies Act 1999 may take deposits. A Bermuda ELP may open settlement accounts with UK or EU-licensed EMIs (for example, Wave, Revolut Business, or Wise) to collect customer payments from Stripe/PayPal and to execute EUR/GBP supplier payments, but such EMIs cannot offer the same counterparty reliability, US clearing access, or capital-es-crow features as Tier-1 Bermudian banks. Legal constraints include the inability of a foreign EMI to conduct regulated banking business in Bermuda without a domestic license, and certain Bermudian banks will not accept EMI-originated Apple-pay/digital-purse funds as 'bank-funded' clearing without enhanced source-of-funds evidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Bermudian banks generally accept a hybrid KYC model: the general partner and any in-scope directors may appear via a live video interview, provided all partners sign via a regulated corporate services provider in Bermuda and documents are notarised and apostilled. However, most banks mandate at least one physical visit of the general partner or a locally registered authorised signatory for the initial capital escrow account; if no travel is possible, a remote onboarding review may be permitted using certified copies, a Bermuda-registered agent interview, and a bank-reference letter from the partner's existing bank. For the operational account, a physical presence is almost always required unless a longstanding relationship with the same banking group exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk merchant category: cross-border e-commerce of jewellery, precious metals, and fine timepieces, with sales routed through Stripe/PayPal and multiple logistics counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified business plan and forecast; completed underwriting pack from Stripe and PayPal evidencing merchant identity, payout bank, and refund policy; invoice-to-cash reconciliation controls; verifiable domain registration, VAT/imports licenses, and business insurance; description of physical inventory flow and proof of commercial storage arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex exempted-partnership make-up: possibility of bearer-interest structures, redelivery of capital, or undisclosed limited partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An up-to-date register of partners certified by the registered agent, LPAs and partnership declaration, legal opinion from Bermuda counsel that no bearer interests exist, source-of-wealth statement from every limited partner, and a confirmation that the ELP is not an 'investment vehicle' for any politically exposed person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment liquidation from third-party processors causing unverifiable trade-cycle funding and potential mixing of customer funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: API-level settlement reports, bank account statements, monthly reconciliation, processor vendor agreements showing the processors solely act as collection agents for the ELP's trade debts, and a funds-flow diagram separating customer proceeds from partner capital injections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reach of UK and US sanctions/anti-money-laundering regimes due to UK Overseas Territory status and USD clearing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions-compliance policy, geo-IP blocking of prohibited countries, OFSI/OFAC screening of every beneficial owner and customer on a rolling basis, evidence that final customers are VAT-registered (when applicable), and a bank-endorsed risk assessment confirming the ELP's foreign exchange flows are derived from lawful online merchandising.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injection of partner capital should be executed via SWIFT MT103 to the ELP's designated BMD or USD account at a Bermudian Tier-1 bank. The remittance information field must explicitly state 'Contribution to capital of an Exempted Limited Partnership' and reference the relevant date of the partners' capital commitment. For non-resident exchange-control status, the inbound wire may carry purpose code 'GIFO' (General investment-fund / capital-transfer) or, if the originating bank requires, 'B100' for capital contributions; the receiving Bermudian bank will verify the remittance against the certified register of partners. Payments in excess of USD 10,000 are automatically screened for source-of-wealth; the contributing partner must provide supporting bank-source documentation and a letter of comfort.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and trade disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to watch manufacturers and gemstone vendors, using same-day settlement via Fedwire/CHIPS for USD and TARGET2 for EUR. For high-value en-gros purchases (e.g., single watch shipments above US$50,000), the Bermudian bank can issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit through MT700, payable at sight against documents. Third-party payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) should be treated only as collection/reconciliation rails, not as disbursement rails; the ELP must also maintain at least one crypto-free fiat liquidity buffer with the Bermudian bank to absorb chargeback volatility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and GBP/EUR up to 12 months tenor backed by actual trade exposure
Express non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies not deliverable in Bermuda, with prior BMA notification when notional exceeds USD 5 million
Cross-currency swaps hedging sales revenue in EUR or GBP against USD-denominated watch purchases
Plain-vanilla FX options (put/call) to cap conversion costs on payouts to overseas suppliers
A Bermuda-dollar/US-dollar constant-neutrality arrangement utilising the BMD/USD pegged parity, subject to bank standard documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exempted Limited Partnership Annual Declaration and Renewal Fee Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual anniversary of the original registration date of the ELP; no calendar-year fixed deadline and no statutory grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment interest accrues on arrears; the ELP is placed on the defaulting partnerships list and may be administratively struck off after 12 months of continuous non-payment; a struck-off ELP cannot enforce contracts, initiate litigation, or maintain its Bermuda banking arrangements until restoration is obtained.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Declaration (ESD) Annual Filing under the Economic Substance Act 2018
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies acting for the Bermuda Economic Substance Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the statutory filing window of 1 January to 31 July for the financial year ended the immediately preceding 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late-filing penalty of US$1,100 plus a daily default penalty of US$50 per day up to a statutory cap; continued non-compliance blocks issuance of tax-residency status confirmations and may be escalated to strike-off proceedings, general partner penalty actions, and referral for prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payroll Tax Monthly Return and Annual Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Tax Commissioner of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the 15th day of the following month on a monthly basis; annual reconciliation is integrated into the December return due by 15 January of the succeeding year. Filing is required only if the ELP employs Bermuda payroll staff; a fully remote e-commerce operation with no Bermuda employees has no filing obligation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues on late remittance at the statutory monthly rate plus a 10% late-payment penalty on the unpaid amount; repeated non-filing may expose the general partner to personal liability for the tax due.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under Bermuda law: the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992 does not impose a size-based statutory audit on an exempted limited partnership. An independent audit becomes mandatory only where the partnership agreement, an investor agreement, or a lending facility requires it, or where a parent group must prepare consolidated audited financial statements under IFRS or US GAAP. The annual Economic Substance Declaration for a non-resident ELP is accepted with unaudited financial information.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is the default international-business framework; US GAAP is equally acceptable where the e-commerce operating group consolidates in USD. The partnership agreement controls the default election, and accounting records must fairly present the transactions, assets, and financial position of the ELP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Bermuda applies an event-driven rather than an annual UBO confirmation protocol: under the Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2017, the ELP and its general partner must file an updated controller return with the Registrar of Companies within 21 days of any transfer of a partnership interest or any change in ultimate beneficial ownership. The anniversary annual declaration separately restates partner composition, creating a de facto annual snapshot for the registry. Transfers of ELP interests remain subject to general-partner consent under the partnership agreement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (name, capital contribution, profit share, admission and transfer dates)
Register of General Partners and Manager appointments
Minute and Resolution Book (partner consents and general partner resolutions)
Register of Controllers maintained under the Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2017

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$2,500 - US$6,500 per annum covering the Bermuda registered office, resident representative, AML and corporate service provider compliance, and regulatory correspondence
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 - US$12,000 per annum only when triggered by an investor, lender, or partnership agreement mandate; not applicable as a statutory audit requirement for a Bermuda ELP

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% general corporate income tax on Bermuda-source and worldwide income for an Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP); 15% Corporate Income Tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 (CITA) applicable only to Constituent Entities of MNE Groups with consolidated revenue of at least USD 750 million, operative for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No income tax, capital gains tax, or VAT in the standard Bermuda regime; the ELP is tax-transparent and profit allocations flow directly to the UK parent. CITA 2023 provides a Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax (QDMTT), a substance-based income exclusion, and a transitional Economic Transition Credit for eligible payroll and fixed-asset expenditure. No statutory tax holidays or preferential rate reductions apply to online jewelry/watch merchandising.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: BRA Form CIT-1 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through the Bermuda Revenue Authority (BRA) electronic filing portal; in-scope MNE Groups also file the GloBE Information Return in accordance with CITA 2023.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (in-scope groups make provisional CIT payments on a quarterly basis)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 15 months after the end of the reporting fiscal year, aligned with the GloBE Information Return cycle; quarterly provisional payments are due in months 3, 6, 9, and 12 of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal name of the Exempted Limited Partnership, Bermuda ELP registration number, and BRA Tax Reference Number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Bermuda ELP registration certificate number; identify the UK parent as the ultimate controlling entity and supply the UK Unique Taxpayer Reference in the attributable-owners schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting fiscal year and consolidation basis: state the fiscal year end and confirm the GloBE consolidated financial statements used for the MNE Group.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the group's consolidated accounts prepared under UK-adopted IFRS; apportion the ELP's results on a look-through basis to the UK parent if the ELP is a transparent entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GloBE Income (Loss) Before Tax: net income or loss per the financial statements adjusted for permanent differences, equity gains, and other GloBE adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reflect only the Bermuda ELP's operations, including online sales gross margin, handling fees, and logistics costs; do not include UK sales booked by the UK parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted Covered Taxes: current and deferred tax expense booked in the financial statements attributable to the ELP's income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bermuda has no general tax charge; zero is entered unless the ELP is within the CITA QDMTT and has booked a QDMTT provision.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Effective Tax Rate and Top-up Tax: compute jurisdictional average ETR, apply the rate differential to excess profit, and deduct the substance-based income exclusion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the payroll and tangible asset carve-outs for the ELP's Bermuda employee headcount and leasehold premises; coordinate with the UK parent's IIR calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax (QDMTT) payable: any top-up tax due to the BRA under CITA 2023.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ELP is a member of an in-scope group, the QDMTT is assessed and payable at the Bermuda ELP level; direct the UK parent not to double-count this amount in IIR filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by General Partner/Authorised Signatory: certification of correctness and completeness.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The designated general partner (often a UK or offshore corporate director) must sign personally; knowingly false declarations attract criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty up to 10% of the tax ultimately due, daily default penalties for continuing failure, and statutory interest on late payment; deliberate inaccuracy attracts civil penalties up to 100% of the understated tax and potential criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration (annual return) filed through the Bermuda Registrar of Companies online portal or the designated registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the ELP's financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity particulars: name, ELP registration number, registered office, and registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the Bermuda registered office and agent; non-resident UK owners do not need to be disclosed individually unless they are general partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax residence declaration: state whether the ELP is tax-resident in Bermuda or in a foreign jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A UK-parented ELP will normally declare residence in the United Kingdom under the limited UK-Bermuda Double Taxation Arrangement or state that it is not resident for CIT purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant Activity: select the applicable category from the Economic Substance Act schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Online retail of jewelry, watches, and fashion goods falls under 'Distribution and Service Centre Business'; select that category even if all sales are processed through Stripe and PayPal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) performed in Bermuda: describe each core function.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide documentary evidence of order-taking, inventory sourcing, logistics coordination, and quality control decisions actually made by Bermuda staff; UK-only performance of these functions is a material red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Employees, premises, and operating expenditure in Bermuda.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State full-time equivalents physically employed in Bermuda, floor space of leased premises, and annual rental and payroll spend; figures inconsistent with revenue volume will trigger an ESR inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of adequacy: confirm that the ELP passes the economic substance test and that the declaration is true.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The general partner must maintain contemporaneous board minutes, invoices, payroll records, and bank statements; the declaration is signed under penalty of perjury.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: initial penalty of BMD 10,000 plus BMD 1,000 per day of continued non-compliance; false or misleading declarations: fines up to BMD 250,000; persistent failure subjects the ELP to strike-off and exchange of information with HMRC.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Bermuda does not impose withholding tax on dividends, distributions, or profit allocations made by an Exempted Limited Partnership to its UK parent or any non-resident partner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Bermuda has no comprehensive double taxation treaty. The UK–Bermuda Double Taxation Arrangement (2013) covers only limited categories of income, principally shipping and air transport, and contains no general dividend, interest, or royalty relief article. The Bermuda Revenue Authority issues a Certificate of Tax Residence upon application, which a UK-resident partner may present for the limited reliefs available. For the ELP's UK-source income, reliance on the arrangement is restricted by its express scope; no standard WHT reclaim procedure exists for partnership distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Bermuda statutory withholding rate on royalties and interest: 0%. UK outbound royalty withholding: 20% statutory rate, typically unreduced because the UK–Bermuda Arrangement lacks a dedicated royalty article; UK interest withholding: 20% statutory rate with numerous domestic exemptions for quoted Eurobonds and bank lending. A UK parent licensing brand or IP into the Bermuda ELP should charge arm's-length royalties and expect 20% UK WHT absent a specific exemption; a Bermuda ELP licensing IP to the UK parent would not suffer Bermuda tax but the UK payer would still be obliged to consider the UK royalty WHT code.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Bermuda CITA 2023 applies only to Constituent Entities of MNE Groups with consolidated revenue of at least BMD 750 million (USD 750 million). Below this threshold, no Bermuda Local File or Master File is statutorily required. For in-scope groups, the BRA may require contemporaneous documentation supporting the arm's-length basis of intercompany transactions, and the GloBE Information Return must be prepared; a UK parent should nevertheless prepare OECD-compliant Master File and Local File because HMRC will assert transfer-pricing documentation obligations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2018, as amended, and the Economic Substance Regulations 2019 require every relevant entity carrying on a relevant activity to maintain adequate economic substance in Bermuda. Online merchandising of jewelry, watches, and fashion goods constitutes a Distribution and Service Centre Business. The ELP must demonstrate (i) management and direction in Bermuda, (ii) a physical office, (iii) suitably qualified full-time employees proportionate to activity, and (iv) minimum operating expenditure in Bermuda. The annual substance declaration is mandatory irrespective of CIT scope; a purely passive or letterbox structure fails the test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsification of e-commerce revenue records, suppression of Stripe/PayPal settlements, fabrication of purchase invoices for jewelry inventory, or misstatement of GloBE income on the BRA CIT-1 return to reduce the 15% CITA charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax, statutory interest, and daily default penalties; criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion carries fines up to BMD 250,000. In the UK, the same profits may attract penalties up to 100% of the tax and the 25% Diverted Profits Tax on artificially diverted UK profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and UK directors may be pursued for fraudulent trading, with civil restitution orders, statutory disqualification under the Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to 7 years for fraudulent evasion of tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Failure of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a brass-plate ELP with no Bermuda office, employees, or board meetings while all distribution, purchasing, and marketing decisions are made by the UK parent; filing a false ESR declaration claiming substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Initial ESR penalty of BMD 10,000 and daily penalties of BMD 1,000; fines up to BMD 250,000 for false declarations; strike-off of the ELP registration; information-sharing notices issued to HMRC under the exchange of information provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Court orders compelling the general partner to restore the ELP to good standing; revocation of the general partner's authorisation; UK parent directors face liability under the UK CFC and DPT rules, including personal liability for penalties where they knowingly approved or tolerated the sham structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing inventory sales from the UK parent to the Bermuda ELP, inflating management fees paid to Bermuda, or booking group marketing and brand royalties offshore without any arm's-length functional analysis; using a circular cash structure to leave profits in Bermuda untaxed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: HMRC transfer-pricing adjustments under TIOPA 2010, application of the 25% Diverted Profits Tax, interest, and penalties up to 100% of the tax charge; for in-scope groups, the BRA may impose QDMTT-based top-up adjustments and the UK parent becomes liable for the GloBE Income Inclusion Rule top-up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incorrect returns or cause the creation of artificial transactions can be personally assessed for penalties under Schedule 24 Finance Act 2007; directors of the ELP general partner can be made personally liable for the diverted profits tax where the corporate veil is pierced for sham pricing arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Sanctions / High-Value Goods Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting third-party card payments through Stripe or PayPal without customer due diligence, processing transactions for sanctioned individuals, deliberate concealment of the beneficial owner of the ELP on the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register, or handling large-value watch sales without source-of-funds checks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the UK Proceeds of Crime Act 2002: unlimited fines and imprisonment up to 14 years for money laundering; under Bermuda's AML/ATF regime: fines up to BMD 1 million per breach, suspension of the ELP's registration, and asset-freeze orders; Stripe/PayPal may terminate payment processing and report to the financial intelligence unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Money Laundering Reporting Officer, general partner, and UK directors face personal criminal liability, seizure of personal assets, travel bans, extradition under the UK–Bermuda Mutual Legal Assistance framework, and disqualification from acting as company directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to appoint a Bermuda registered agent, omission to file the annual ESR declaration, refusal to produce books and records to the BRA or HMRC, late payment of provisional CIT without reasonable excuse, or obstruction of a tax inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Daily default penalties for non-filing, judicial restoration procedures, and strike-off of the ELP; HMRC failure-to-notify penalties up to 100% of the tax due, information notices enforceable by the First-tier Tribunal, and search and seizure under the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers can be made personally liable for penalties where non-compliance is attributable to their consent or neglect; the general partner may be sued by limited partners for unlawful distributions, and civil recovery proceedings may compel directors to restore misapplied funds, subject to travel restrictions pending final judgment.
